Reaction (A):  
Cyclohexene is converted into 8,8-diiodobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one.  This product is obtained by a [2 + 2] cycloaddition of a ketene to the C=C bond of cyclohexene, giving a fused cyclobutanone in which the two iodines reside on the same carbon (C-8).  
The reagent that supplies a two-carbon C=C=O unit bearing two iodines on the terminal carbon is 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one (diiodoketene).  
Thus, A = 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one.

Reactivity order of the dienes (B):  
For Diels–Alder reactions, the most reactive dienes are those that (i) are locked in the s-cis conformation and (ii) have electron-donating substituents that raise the HOMO energy, while steric hindrance to the s-cis form decreases reactivity.

1. Cyclopenta-1,3-diene (3) – permanently locked in the s-cis form; highest reactivity.  
2. 2,3-Dimethylbuta-1,3-diene (1) – two electron-donating Me groups raise the HOMO; although some steric hindrance exists, it is still quite reactive.  
3. (2E,4E)-Hexa-2,4-diene (2) – can adopt s-cis, but requires rotation and has no extra activation; less reactive than 1.  
4. (2Z,4Z)-Hexa-2,4-diene (4) – the Z,Z geometry causes severe allylic steric crowding in the s-cis form, making it the least reactive.

Hence the decreasing order of reactivity is: 3 > 1 > 2 > 4.

Among the choices, only option (C) gives both the correct reactant A and the correct order B.

Answer: C
